name: Neo-Legionarism
summary: Neo-Legionarism is the post-1989 Romanian movement of groups that claim the tradition of Corneliu Zelea Codreanu's Legion of the Archangel Michael (the Iron Guard). Its ideology fuses fascism, ethnic nationalism, anti-Semitism, Romanian folklore, mysticism and Orthodox Christianity, and it venerates Codreanu and the Legion's martyrs. Through Codreanu's own texts it rejects democracy and parties for rule by a selected elite under a monarch, subordinates the individual to an eternal nation of the living and the dead, and seeks a spiritual rebirth and a 'new man'.
scope: The defining scholarship presents neo-Legionarism as groups that, after 1989, 'defined themselves as Legionary, thereby entering into the tradition of the Iron Guard' founded by Codreanu, expressing their message 'mainly ... through references to Codreanu's movement' (Endresen, s6), and that 'promoted principles promoted by Legionary Movement's leader, Corneliu Codreanu' (Simion, s7). The profile therefore answers from those scholarly accounts and from Codreanu's own canonical texts, For My Legionaries (s2) and The Nest Leader's Manual (s10). It does not answer from the programmes of individual organisations (Noua Dreapta, Everything for the Country, the Movement for Romania) or from parties such as AUR, and the interwar Legion's brief rule in 1940-41 is not neo-Legionarism's record.

sources.title: The Nest Leader's Manual (Cărticica șefului de cuib), English translation
sources.author: Corneliu Zelea Codreanu
sources.usedFor: The Legion's handbook (1933): the six laws of the nest, education of youth and girls' nests, elections, the Legionary against the politician, the communist and the Jew, the new man, parliamentary rules and the commandments.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The army is honoured as a school of the nation, so abolishing it is rejected.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The creed keeps workers, tradesmen and national unions organised by occupation, so the division of labour stays.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Codreanu calls 'the system of privileges through birth' 'unjust and condemned' and wants the elite chosen by selection, not heredity, though he keeps the monarchy (For My Legionaries).

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The 1920 creed reproduced in For My Legionaries calls for 'a progressive income tax'.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The creed itself pays wages and salaries, and the movement is anti-communist.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement stresses order and authority.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The 1920 creed sets wages and salaries by work and family size and keeps owners alongside workers, so wage labour stays (For My Legionaries).

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The 1920 creed calls for 'distributing the land among all the ploughmen', and Codreanu's first ideals include raising the peasantry through land reform, not state ownership of land (For My Legionaries).

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Codreanu speaks of Romanians reconquering Transylvania 'following 1000 years of Hungarian occupation', treating an annexation as lasting occupation (For My Legionaries).

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Legion's death teams and revolutionary violence reflect a belief that a small committed group can force change.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Codreanu tells how as a schoolboy he and his comrades swore that if the Bolshevik army crossed the Dniester they would 'take refuge in the woods armed' and organise Romanian resistance (For My Legionaries).

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: For My Legionaries reproduces with approval Conta's rule that citizenship should go only to foreigners 'who assimilate or are inclined to do so by marriage', and counts the Jews as a danger because they do not assimilate.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Codreanu denounces the dissolution of the Guard 'in defiance of laws and Constitution' and asks whether democracy can claim 'that a people is not free to decide its own destiny, to change its Constitution, its form of government' (For My Legionaries).

bound-labor.rationale: The creed gives land to those who plough it rather than binding them to a lord.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Codreanu's first charge against democracy is that it 'breaks the unity of the Romanian people, dividing it into parties', and he says the politician lives 'under the tyranny ... of the electoral agent' (For My Legionaries).

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Codreanu defends driving Yiddish plays off Romania's stages as 'national demoralization and moral decadence' and says it was 'the duty of ... the government, or any authority' to act against them (For My Legionaries).

citizens-assembly.rationale: The movement rejects democratic deliberation as divisive.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Codreanu objects that democracy made Jews, settled for 'hardly 100, 10, or 5 years', Romanian citizens, and reproduces Conta's rule that citizenship belongs to those of the nation's blood or who join it by marriage (For My Legionaries).

class-collaboration.rationale: The creed's aim is social harmony and cooperation of owners and workers.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The creed seeks 'social harmony through minimizing of class differences', and Codreanu wants workers to win their rights 'within the framework of the state and not against the state' (For My Legionaries).

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Codreanu's movement campaigned in Bessarabia and his creed claims one state for all Romanians 'from Dniester to the Tisa' (For My Legionaries).

collective-farming.rationale: The creed distributes land among individual ploughmen and defends the peasant smallholder, not collective farms.

conscription.rationale: The creed treats military service as a school of the nation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority comes from the Captain and the nation's mission, not consent.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Codreanu rejects parliamentary democracy, so a democratically elected assembly is not their route to a constitution.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Codreanu lists 'poverty, namely voluntary renunciation of amassing a fortune' among the foundations of the elite, and the Nest Leader's Manual calls for an aristocracy of virtue resting on no money, wealth or clothes.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The creed envisages a strong unified state, not small cooperatives.

corporate-influence.rationale: Codreanu: 'Democracy is in the service of great finance' and 'becomes the slave of the great Jewish international finance which subjugates it by subvention' (For My Legionaries).

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The creed has national unions with representatives on the administrative boards of firms, a corporatist design.

culture-before-state.rationale: Codreanu's creed aims first at spiritual rebirth and the moral formation of a new man, with political power following, though the movement also seeks a state.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: For My Legionaries calls Judaism's concept of life 'a cultural monstrosity' to be eliminated and holds that the Jewish nation is sterile in culture, ranking cultures rather than treating them as equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Codreanu's first demand in Parliament was 'the introduction of the death penalty for the fraudulent manipulators of public funds', defended against a theology professor: 'I prefer the death of the thief' (For My Legionaries).

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The creed's social provisions (risk fund, storehouses, homes for the old) point against cutting welfare, though it was written for citizens only.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Manual: 'The legionnaire is against communism and fight with all your might', since its triumph would abolish monarchy, Church, family, property and freedom.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Internationalist class politics is condemned; workers are to organise nationally and support their nation.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Fierce anti-communism is central to the Legion, so a communist planned state is not defended whoever rules it.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: Codreanu writes that in a democracy man loses his rights 'in favor of a politico-financier caste of bankers and electoral agents' and that democracy becomes 'the slave of the great Jewish international finance' (For My Legionaries).

democracy-best.rationale: Codreanu: democracy was excluded and he lived anti-democracy from the start; the democratic setup is a curse on the people.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Codreanu rejects the clash of parties: under democracy 'one party nullifies the plans and the efforts of another', so it is 'incapable of continuity in effort' (For My Legionaries).

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement rejects democracy as a harm, so spreading it is not seen as beneficial.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Manual counts the triumph of communism in Romania as the abolition of 'monarchy, ... Church, ... Family, ... individual property and ... freedom', which the Legionary must fight.

direct-action.rationale: Split: the Nest Leader's Manual trains nests to win elections and seat Legionary deputies, while Codreanu also defends the 1923 plot to shoot ministers and says a real elite is born of war with the false one (For My Legionaries).

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Codreanu rejected elections and put authority in a chosen leader rather than votes.

direct-votes.rationale: Split: Codreanu says truth cannot be put to a majority vote, yet holds that the multitude 'ought to be consulted before the great decisions that affect its future' (For My Legionaries).

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Split: the 1920 creed gives 'equal rights, both civil and political, to men and to women', while the Nest Leader's Manual organises women separately and trains girls for motherhood and the home.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The creed links pay to both work and number of children, mixing need and effort.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: For My Legionaries quotes with approval that different races in one state, if not assimilated, lead to 'perpetual struggles between opposite tendencies' and a 'fight for existence between two races'.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Codreanu says a people is led not by its will nor one man's but by natural laws, and that 'to each nation God has traced a line of destiny' the monarch must follow (For My Legionaries).

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Codreanu says God gave a mission 'to us Romanians ... as to any other people in the world' and that all peoples will be resurrected each in its place, while For My Legionaries rejects the Jewish idea of a chosen people.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual: before the country 'the legionnaire is presented not civil rights, but the sacred debt'; Codreanu also subordinates the individual to the national collectivity and the nation (For My Legionaries).

dynastic-succession.rationale: Codreanu defends hereditary monarchy as always good ('I reject the republic'), though he rejects heredity as the basis of the governing elite (For My Legionaries).

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Its ethnic nationalism and antisemitism include demands that Romanians, not minorities such as Jews, control the nation's economic life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The creed asks the educated to descend among the tired and humble, implying they are detached from them.

elective-rulers.rationale: Codreanu rejected elections and chose leaders himself.

elite-replacement.rationale: Codreanu says Romania's leaders 'betrayed their people' to finance while 'the beginning of Jewish existence on our soil foreshadowed the death of Romanians; that as their numbers increased, we would die' (For My Legionaries).

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Codreanu backs numerus clausus, limiting Jews in schools and professions by ethnic proportion, and calls it an inadequate first measure (For My Legionaries).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Codreanu holds that 'Human rights' are 'no longer unlimited, but limited by the rights of national collectivity' and that a people must be free to change its constitution as it pleases (For My Legionaries).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Codreanu rejects equal rights for Jews in the state: 'Equality? On what basis? ... equality means treating unequal things unequally' (For My Legionaries, 'Several observations regarding democracy').

equal-outcomes.rationale: The creed narrows class differences but ties pay to work and family size.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The 1920 creed wants a state that is 'the holder of all Romanians and only of Romanians', and Codreanu reproduces approvingly that naturalisation should go only to foreigners who assimilate into 'the blood of the dominant race' (For My Legionaries).

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: Codreanu concludes that 'a people is not capable of governing itself' and must be led by an elite, so democracy suits no people, Romania included (For My Legionaries).

experts-over-public.rationale: Codreanu argues that leading a nation needs specialised aptitudes like any trade, that the multitude cannot know the laws of leadership, and that a people must be governed by its elite rather than by itself (For My Legionaries, 'Election, selection, heredity').

family-wage.rationale: The 1920 creed reproduced in For My Legionaries pays workers and public servants 'on the basis of the number of children and the work performed'.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The creed endorses a progressive income tax.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Codreanu demanded in Parliament that 'the territory of Romania be declared the inalienable and indefeasible property of the Romanian Nation', and invokes the constitutional ban on colonisation by people of foreign origin (For My Legionaries).

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The 1919 appeal Codreanu reproduces warns that 'the enemies in the East have united with those in the West to disturb our peace so they can invade us', attacking 'at the Dniester and at the Tisa' (For My Legionaries).

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Codreanu rejects giving Jews 'political rights equal to those of Romanians' and denounces the treaty that granted them 'political rights en masse' (For My Legionaries).

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: For My Legionaries describes democracy as letting in 'foreigners with money, as coming to buy bankrupt stores' so that 'the country is auctioned off', and demands the expulsion of foreign exploiters of Romania's riches.

future-generations.rationale: Codreanu condemns 'the pitiless exploitation and the alienation of our forests, mines, oil reserves, forgetting that there are hundreds of Romanian generations ... who likewise expect to live' (For My Legionaries).

gradual-change.rationale: The Manual says the new state cannot be built with 'old people' and needs a whole people's 'great revolution of mind', not piecemeal reform.

hereditarian-race.rationale: For My Legionaries sets out, as Cuza's 'science of anti-Semitism' that Codreanu adopts, that the Jews' 'sterility ... in the domain of culture' results from their being 'a mixture of unrelated races', an inherited explanation of a group's ability.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Codreanu bases Romania's right on being the one people 'born in the mist of time on this land', unlike the Bulgarians, Turks and Magyars who came later (For My Legionaries, 'We and our land').

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Codreanu's first ideal is 'the unification of the Romanian people' in one state, 'from Dniester to the Tisa' (For My Legionaries).

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Codreanu: Romanians are bound to their land 'not only by the bread ... but also by all the bones of our ancestors who sleep in its ground' (For My Legionaries, 'We and our land').

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: For My Legionaries welcomes foreigners such as Russians, Greeks, Italians and Germans who 'intermarry and fuse with us' but not those who stay apart.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The creed pays by work performed and shrinks owners' returns relative to their investment.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Codreanu holds that rights belong also to 'the present national collectivity' and to 'the nation', and that individual rights are 'limited by the rights of national collectivity, these in turn being limited by those of the nation' (For My Legionaries).

informal-organisation.rationale: The Legion was a disciplined hierarchy under a single leader, not informal groups.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Codreanu asks whether the 'clothes of democracy' suit Romanians, says they should be kept 'if for us they are suitable ... even if all Europe should discard them', and finds they are not (For My Legionaries).

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1920 creed proposed distributing land among all the ploughmen.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The creed distributes land to individual ploughmen as holders, not communal tenure.

leader-cult.rationale: The Manual sets out a ceremonial order for receiving the Head of the Legion, and Veridica reports neo-Legionaries' yearly commemorations of Codreanu and a cult of the movement's emblematic figures.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nest meetings speak of 'the martyrs, heroes who died' and pray for their souls (Nest Leader's Manual); neo-Legionaries hold commemorations of Legionary 'martyrs' (Veridica) and cultivate the Prison Saints cult (Marincea).

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Codreanu puts the spiritual patrimony above the physical and material ones ('not bread, but honor at any price') and makes the resurrection of peoples in Christ the final aim of nations (For My Legionaries).

means-match-ends.rationale: Codreanu stressed that the Legion's moral conduct and self-reform must precede changing the nation.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual organises the Legion in nests under commanders with ranks, uniforms, orders and strict discipline ('Follow your head for better or worse').

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Codreanu calls the Marmorosch Blank bank a 'Judaic nest of conspiracy and corruption' and describes Jewish 'plans' to take over commerce and politics, and the Manual calls the Jewish problem the greatest danger in Romanian history.

minority-veto.rationale: The Legion put unity and discipline above dissent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Codreanu rejects the parliamentary balance of forces and wants unified leadership.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sacrifice for the nation and duty over gain is the Legion's ethos, though the creed also pays wages.

more-religion-public.rationale: For the Legionary 'politics is religion' (Nest Leader's Manual), Codreanu sets the nation's final aim as 'the resurrection of peoples in the name of the Savior Jesus Christ' (For My Legionaries), and Endresen describes the movement's ideology as fused with Orthodox Christianity.

nation-first.rationale: For Codreanu the nation's leaders must act on its 'historic honor, its eternal interests', 'not bread, but honor at any price', and fascism means 'defending your nation against the dangers that threaten it' (For My Legionaries).

national-law-over-international.rationale: For My Legionaries sides with Cuza in calling the peace treaty's 'minorities' clause' 'an impermissible meddling into our national affairs'.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual calls for 'a great nation requires renewed spiritual renewal', a 'new man' and 'the clock's resurrection as a nation', the founding idea of the Legion.

national-resource-control.rationale: Codreanu condemns the 'pitiless exploitation and the alienation of our forests, mines, oil reserves' and demanded in Parliament 'the expulsion of the hordes of pitiless exploiters who have come here to drain the riches from our soil' (For My Legionaries).

national-self-determination.rationale: Codreanu holds that God gave every people 'a mission, a historic destiny', and his first ideal is the union of all Romanians in one state (For My Legionaries).

native-born-offices.rationale: The creed makes the state one of Romanians and only Romanians.

natural-rulers.rationale: Codreanu: 'A people is not capable of governing itself. It ought to be governed by its elite', men born with 'certain aptitudes and specialties' (For My Legionaries).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Codreanu fights communism and also 'an oligarchic and tyrannical class' that skins the workers and 'great Jewish international finance', under the name 'National-Christian Socialism' (For My Legionaries).

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Codreanu recounts carrying a revolver and firing at the police prefect Manciu after the Legion's members were beaten, and justifies resistance by force to those who 'kill us' (For My Legionaries).

night-watchman-state.rationale: The creed gives the state a wide role in welfare, economy and morals, far beyond a minimal state.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Codreanu attacked the Marmorosch Blank bank's loans to leading politicians and demanded that politicians be barred from the boards of banks and financial enterprises (For My Legionaries).

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Legion is organised as a Christian movement whose meetings open with prayer and for which 'politics is religion' (Nest Leader's Manual).

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Legion defied the state yet demanded total obedience from members; adherents reject a general freedom from obedience.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Codreanu: 'this territory is the inalienable and indefeasible property of the Romanian people ... even thousands of years later we will claim the right over this land' (For My Legionaries).

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The creed asks educated and better-off Romanians to go among the tired and humble.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Codreanu's monarch must avoid 'the line of personal interest or that of a class of people or group' and follow only that of his people (For My Legionaries, 'Monarchy and the law of monarchy').

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Codreanu chose his followers himself and wanted a ruling elite of moral soldiers, the opposite of random selection.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Manual says the Legion will replace 'governments and parties' with 'an Iron Guard government' and that the country should be run by the Guard, and Codreanu blames parties for dividing the nation (For My Legionaries).

open-borders.rationale: Codreanu invokes the constitution's rule that 'the territory of Romania cannot be colonized by a population of foreign origin' against Jewish settlement (For My Legionaries).

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Codreanu recounts the 1923 student plot to assassinate ministers and bankers and his own shooting of the prefect Manciu, presenting both as justified (For My Legionaries).

organic-representation.rationale: The creed gives national unions seats on administrative boards and abolishes the Senate for organized representation.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Codreanu rejected parliamentary democracy as a curse.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement rejects democracy and rule by assemblies.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Codreanu's Legion required strict obedience and he avoided voting.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Manual's youth nests teach that the young Romanian 'must love his motherland, the Earth and the King', and Codreanu wants the school, theatre and church to raise the nation's consciousness (For My Legionaries).

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Codreanu's Legion appealed to peasants and workers on national and Orthodox grounds, joining patriotism with a politics for ordinary people.

pay-for-effort.rationale: The 1920 creed pays workers according to 'the work performed, quality and quantity' as well as family size (For My Legionaries).

people-in-arms.rationale: The creed keeps a standing army that trains conscripts for a year, so it does not replace it with an armed populace.

person-over-state.rationale: Codreanu: 'The individual must be subordinated to the superior entity, the national collectivity, which in turn must be subordinated to the nation' (For My Legionaries).

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Followers swear loyalty to the Captain, a personal rather than institutional authority.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: Codreanu called Legionaries to build a dam with their own arms in work camps as a school for the masses, and the Manual's 'Labour Law' reads 'Work every day. Work with love.'

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Codreanu calls the party system a curse and says parties are tools of Jewish power; elite corruption is a central theme.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Manual sets the Legionary who comes 'for God's sake' against those who buy souls 'in the name of Satan'; Endresen writes that neo-Legionaries believe 'transcendental forces influence life on earth'.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Codreanu blames Jewish exploitation and the party system for peasant poverty, not population growth.

population-transfer.rationale: For My Legionaries demands 'the expulsion of the hordes of pitiless exploiters' and adopts as the conclusion of anti-Semitism 'the elimination of Jews from the midst of other people'.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Unitary-state nationalism favours one national community in power.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Codreanu names the nation's culture part of its 'spiritual patrimony', 'the expression of national genius', and says 'A people must defend all three' patrimonies, the spiritual one above all (For My Legionaries, 'The nation').

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Codreanu writes that in a democracy 'money, press and votes determine life and death' and that the individual's rights are lost to 'a politico-financier caste of bankers and electoral agents' (For My Legionaries).

priority-to-poor.rationale: The creed prioritizes peasants and workers, and Codreanu frames the movement as defending them against exploitation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A nationalist movement with a strong state ideal does not privatize courts or defense.

production-for-use.rationale: The creed keeps private initiative and returns to owners, so profit remains.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Codreanu notes approvingly that 'the greater and more civilized European nations' have discarded democracy and calls it the system 'which I see killing the Romanian people' (For My Legionaries).

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: For My Legionaries calls for 'the elimination of Jews from the midst of other people' and denies them the citizenship granted to them, including those long settled in Romania.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The 1920 creed ties pay to the number of children, a financial support for larger families, and Codreanu treats foreign settlement as colonisation to be stopped (For My Legionaries).

property-fundamental.rationale: The creed backs private initiative only where it serves the nation, which makes property subordinate to national interest.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The creed encourages private initiative in the interest of the nation.

public-ownership.rationale: The early creed called for nationalizing factories, but later Legionary and neo-Legionary writing is mostly silent on economics.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Codreanu treats the settlement of Jews, defined by descent as 'a mixture of unrelated races', as an invasion to be stopped, while accepting other foreigners who assimilate (For My Legionaries).

race-social-construct.rationale: For My Legionaries treats races as real descent groups, citing 'anthropology' that Jews are 'a mixture of unrelated races' and seeking a state 'of the same single blood'.

racial-community-economic-control.rationale: Codreanu wants commerce, industry and the towns taken back from Jews by Romanians ('Let the Romanian become a merchant'), treating each people's control of its economy as a national necessity (For My Legionaries, 'The Jewish problem').

racial-franchise.rationale: For My Legionaries opposes 'the minorities' clause' that granted Jews 'political rights en masse' and asks 'On what basis do the Jews demand equal treatment, political rights equal to those of Romanians?'

racial-group-interests.rationale: Codreanu frames politics as Romanians uniting against 'the united block of the Judaic power' and quotes approvingly that peoples sharing one state end in 'a fight for existence between two races' (For My Legionaries).

racial-pride.rationale: Codreanu calls national culture 'the expression of national genius, of the blood', and the Nest Leader's Manual wants the new man to gather 'all the qualities of our race'.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual makes prayer 'a decisive element of victory' and tells the Legionary to believe in God and call on the ancestors' souls, rejecting reason as the only guide.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Captain principle subordinates followers to the leader, not the other way.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Codreanu calls Jewish settlement in Romania an 'invasion' and 'colonization' barred by the constitution, and demanded 'the expulsion of the hordes of pitiless exploiters' (For My Legionaries).

regulate-corporations.rationale: The 1920 creed in For My Legionaries has the state share profits between owners and workers and seat union representatives on company boards, and Codreanu's 1931 demands bar politicians from the boards of banks and financial firms; it is an early text.

religion-illusion.rationale: Codreanu holds that peoples are 'realities even in the nether world' and will be resurrected 'each people having its place before God's throne' (For My Legionaries), the opposite of religion as an illusion.

religious-nation.rationale: Codreanu counts the nation's 'concept of God' in its spiritual patrimony and fights 'for our Romanian and Christian faith' (For My Legionaries); Endresen finds ethnic nationalism fused with Orthodoxy in neo-Legionary ideology.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: For My Legionaries adopts 'the elimination of Jews from the midst of other people', but accepts Russians, Greeks, Italians and Germans who intermarry and fuse with Romanians.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Manual's parliamentary rules give a Legionary deputy's allowance to the Legion, which pays him only enough 'for a modest existence', since 'You can not slap a salary of 30,000 lei per month luxury' on the country's misery.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Legion resisted what it saw as an illegitimate regime, so resistance to a ruler is accepted.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The Manual's law of honour says it is better 'to fall on the road fighting honor' than accept disgrace, and its ninth commandment says the Legionary 'loves death, for his blood will serve' the Guard.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Codreanu invokes the constitutional rule that 'the territory of Romania cannot be colonized by a population of foreign origin' on behalf of Romanians as the land's original people (For My Legionaries).

return-lost-territory.rationale: For My Legionaries holds that even 'thousands of years later we will claim the right over this land, as we reconquered the Transylvanian land'.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: 'The unification of the Romanian people' is the first of the three ideals Codreanu takes from Iorga and Cuza, and the creed wants one undivided state 'from Dniester to the Tisa' (For My Legionaries).

right-to-secede.rationale: The creed demands one undivided state and the movement seeks a restored Greater Romania.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Codreanu's solution to the Jewish problem is that they leave, not that they seek equal rights.

rule-by-example.rationale: Codreanu led by moral example and demanded self-reform before reform of others.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement idealises the peasant and Orthodox village and laments the decay of cities.

sacred-nation.rationale: For Codreanu the nation includes 'all the souls of our dead and the tombs of our ancestors' and 'all those who will be born Romanians', and lives beyond this earth (For My Legionaries, 'The nation').

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Codreanu fought to keep the national theatres for 'the national and moral education of the Romanian people' and calls the nation's culture an eternal patrimony to defend (For My Legionaries).

second-chamber.rationale: The 1920 creed reproduced in For My Legionaries calls for 'the abolition of the Senate'.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Sacrifice for the nation is the ethos; Codreanu calls on followers to die for the people.

separate-church-state.rationale: The creed wants a state 'in fear of God' with 'one Sacred Christian Church', and Codreanu makes the resurrection of the nation in Christ its final aim (For My Legionaries).

separated-powers.rationale: The creed removes the Senate and favors strong centralized leadership.

simple-living.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual has Legionary deputies hand their pay to the Legion and live modestly in common barracks rather than in luxury, and Codreanu makes voluntary poverty a mark of the elite (For My Legionaries).

single-common-good.rationale: The Legion sees a single national good and calls pluralist parties a curse.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The 1919 appeal in For My Legionaries reminds soldiers that they 'took an oath to defend with your blood to the last drop the fatherland's borders', and the Manual likens the Legionary's sacrifice to a soldier's on the battlefield.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Codreanu: a nation has a physical, a material and a spiritual patrimony, and 'the most important however is its spiritual patrimony, for only it carries the stamp of eternity' (For My Legionaries).

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis; the movement is anti-communist and sees the state as the nation's instrument.

state-harmful.rationale: The Legion wanted a stronger, purified Romanian state, not its abolition (the creed speaks of one undivided state).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Manual wants youth kept 'free of communist literature that stands against God' and educated to love God and live by Christian teaching.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual says the new state needs 'a new type of man' formed in all the virtues, and Codreanu wants the theatre, school and church to raise the nation morally (For My Legionaries).

strong-leader.rationale: Codreanu says he never put propositions to a vote and chose his followers himself; the Captain principle is the movement's core.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The creed endorsed a progressive income tax; modern groups add little on tax.

taxation-theft.rationale: Codreanu's 1920 creed endorses a progressive income tax, so taxation is treated as legitimate.

traditional-family.rationale: The 1920 creed makes the state 'protector of the family', and the Nest Leader's Manual counts the abolition of the family among communism's chief evils and prepares girls to be mothers.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: For My Legionaries: 'Only one people came from nowhere: ours. We were born in the mist of time on this land together with the oaks and fir trees.'

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Manual organises the Brotherhoods of the Cross for youths of 14 to 20 with physical training for 'the soldier of tomorrow' and uniforms; Veridica records neo-Legionary youth and boot camps.

unions-good.rationale: Codreanu organised national unions of workers, but as nationalist bodies opposed to Marxist unions, so support is conditional.

vanguard-party.rationale: Codreanu's Legion was an elite of moral soldiers leading the masses.

vote-delegation.rationale: The movement rejects democratic mechanisms generally.

war-builds-character.rationale: Codreanu's death teams and cult of sacrifice treat struggle and death as national regeneration.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement attacks Jewish finance and big money.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The creed's social benefits are for Romanians only, since the state is the holder of Romanians and only Romanians.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The creed distributes land among ploughmen and Codreanu defends the peasant and middle class against Jewish commerce.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Legion made political struggle a sacred duty, not a thing to avoid.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1920 creed gives women 'equal rights, both civil and political' with men (For My Legionaries).

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1920 creed reproduced in For My Legionaries makes the state 'giver of equal rights, both civil and political, to men and to women'.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: The Nest Leader's Manual makes work one of the six fundamental laws of the nest ('Work every day') and wants the Legionary to build the new Romania by his own work.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Codreanu's movement appealed jointly to 'tradesmen, workers, soldiers and peasants' and draws its elite from 'the large healthy mass of peasantry and workingmen' (For My Legionaries).

workers-councils.rationale: Anti-communist and committed to national unions under national leadership.

workers-nation.rationale: Codreanu organised national unions of Romanian workers against Marxist internationalism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The creed has worker representation but under national leadership, not company votes.

missingStatements.text: Those who die for the nation should be honoured as martyrs and saints.
missingStatements.rationale: The Prison Saints devotion and Legionary martyr cult make sacrificial death a sacred, public national honour.

missingStatements.text: Politics is fundamentally a spiritual struggle between good and evil.
missingStatements.rationale: Described as viewing politics as a spiritual battle with a revelation from Archangel Michael to Codreanu.

notes: Later pass (rules 5) by claude-opus-5-5. The first pass rested largely on Wikipedia (s1, s3) and on Noua Dreapta's platform; this pass nulled every answer that had no other evidence and re-answered from Codreanu's two canonical texts (For My Legionaries and The Nest Leader's Manual, read in full for each theme) and the scholarship that ties them to neo-Legionarism. Answers resting on the 1920 creed reproduced in For My Legionaries are an early text and carry at most medium confidence. The scholarship that lists neo-Legionaries' modern positions (Endresen 2010, whose abstract alone is open; it is the source Wikipedia cites for opposition to the EU, NATO, the UN, immigration, homosexuality, abortion and drugs) is paywalled (CEEOL, academia.edu login), so those statements are null; Andreescu's Extremismul de dreapta in Romania (2003) was read but does not name neo-Legionarism and is not cited. Themes searched: economy (creed, land, unions, finance), government (democracy, elite, monarchy, parties, elections), society and culture (nation, race, religion, family, education), world (territory, minorities clause, communism, invasion), liberty (rights, death penalty, censorship), means (violence, revolution, work camps). Ecology, technology, globalism and most modern social issues have no source.
